thread.title_full: Expansion of Jack's Oyster House brand grows in scope - NewsBreak

author: Steve Barnes
title: Expansion of Jack's Oyster House brand grows in scope - NewsBreak
text:
By Steve Barnes ,
12 hours ago The promised revival of Jack’s Oyster House in Albany may be long in the future, but the new owner, NeoVista Equities, is expanding the brand downtown with a deli due by the end of this year, as well as concepts called Jack’s Steakhouse and Smoothies by Jack’s. The company also is developing NeoVista Fresh Market, a downtown grocery store unaffiliated with The Fresh Market chain. (Will Waldron/Times Union) ALBANY — Two food concepts from NeoVista Equities, a downstate real estate company moving rapidly into the local market with purchases including Jack’s Oyster House, are projected to open downtown in the coming months, according to a NeoVista representative. The promised revival of the legendary oyster house and additional restaurant projects remain further in the future, the representative said.
Jack’s Deli, with an official address of 41 State St., across from Jack’s Oyster House at 44 State but with an entrance around the corner on Broadway, has had demolition and construction permits approved and should be open by the end of the year, said Flerida Santana Johnas, regional director for NeoVista Equities. The company, based in Long Island, bought the Jack’s Oyster House building and a five-story property on nearby James Street earlier this year.
Jack’s Deli will be built in two contiguous leased spaces — one a former office, the other now-closed restaurants including OkiPoki and Dali Mamma. NeoVista says it will serve “authentic New York-style sandwiches & fresh deli classics”; the minimal website for Jack’s Deli says, “From time-honored classics to bold signature creations, we bring together fresh ingredients, traditional recipes, and a whole lot of heart.”
Opening soon after, Johnas said, perhaps by the end of the year or early in 2026, depending on permitting, will be NeoVista Fresh Market, unaffiliated with The Fresh Market grocery chain that has two Capital Region locations. Being developed at the 52 James St. property, NeoVista Fresh Market will sell organic produce, “wholesome foods,” grab-and-go prepared fare, pantry staples, desserts made famous in New York City bakeries and products to support sustainable living, according to its Facebook and Instagram pages. They include the detail that the market will offer delivery. NeoVista has previously said it it will use other floors of 52 James St. for its Capital Region headquarters and for a day care business.
Additional concepts expanding the Jack’s brand that are mentioned on the Jack’s Restaurant Group website , but with no addresses or time frames, are Jack’s Steakhouse ; Smoothies by Jack’s ; and Bian Dang by Jack’s , described as making grab-and-go box lunches, including halal and vegan options, to be sold in NeoVista Fresh Market and Smoothies by Jack’s. In Mandarin, “bian dang” means “convenience” and refers to prepared meals akin to Japanese bento boxes.
NeoVista was also involved in a battle in the spring to acquire 60 S. Pearl St., a four-story, 35,000-square-foot building that currently houses the county Department of Probation. In May, the Albany County Legislature was within hours of voting to sell the property to a busy downtown developer, over the objections of legislators who believed NeoVista’s offer was unfairly overlooked, when County Executive Dan McCoy retracted the proposal, blaming a “media frenzy.”
McCoy’s office said it would restart the bidding process for 60 S. Pearl St. NeoVista wants to use the building for a 30- to 40-room boutique hotel and retail storefronts; its competitor, Liberty Park Development, said it would create street-level retail and about 30 apartments on upper floors, calling the 60 S. Pearl project a “vitally important” component of its expansive vision for the nearby proposed Liberty Square , which would include a soccer stadium, retail and commercial space and a total of 1,000 apartments.
